[quote=sal-baliz;59675860][b]Ocean hijacking[/b]

The Sal-Baliz corvette Rawuwf waits in the Baliwick sea for it's prey. Details of an Orphogronian uranium shipment have once again be provided to the Sal-Baliz and soon they are to be "hijacked". That was the plan anyway, but at around 10:20pm an odd vessel appeared on the foggy horizon. It first appeared as s military patrol boat, causing panic among the Sal-Baliz. Immediately missiles were fired. The missiles hit the front of the appraoching ship, causing it to begin to sink. The Rawuwf speeds towards the rapidly sinking ship in order to capture hostages, but they soon discover that the ship is a small civilian speedboat, even better. The small vessel is promptly boarded. The people on board appear to be from the ULR, possibly fishermen. They put up a small fight, but are no match for the unmerciful Sal-Baliz soldiers. The personnel of the boat is rounded up, a grand total of 5 people, all close friends by the looks of it. The men are made to put their hands behind their heads so that the Sal-Baliz can make a broadcast. An old camera from the late 80s is used to film the helpless fishermen, who all have multiple rifles pointed to their heads.

[i]"To the ULR government, these are your people and if you want them back I suggest you comply with what we are about to ask. First, we want your word that you will not trade or be involved in any way with THEP or it's members. Secondly, you will end the persecution of Muslims within your borders, or face the might of Al-Qadi. Third and finally, you shall send us 200,000 barrels of oil and a sum of 1,000,000,000 tabuhts immediately. Comply and your people will return safely, disobey and they will die, simple. You have 72 hours."[/i]

The recording cuts out and is broadcast directly to the ULR government. Whilst the Sal-Baliz wait for a response, the hostages are being transported back into Sal-Baliz territory and being held in a prison cell. Another ship has been deployed to receive the uranium.

Late in the night, a young man is walking home in the city of Aduab. Sitting down on a streetcorner, he opens his bottle of soda and takes a sip. Even though he should go home, he feels something big will happen, and he's right. Looking up, a full moon helps illuminate a small plane looking thing in the sky as it flies overhead and then out of sight overhead the buildings around him. He wonders for a second what it could have possibly been, and then a blast booms through the night silence, answering his question. He stands in shock for a few seconds before another blast goes off, bringing him back to reality. Thinking quickly, he rushes to the closest building with a basement he knows of which is his local hospital. Arriving, the staff enlist him and whoever they can into helping them move patients to the basement throughout the night. As the sun comes up the next morning, the blasts have stopped and the hospital is fine. Checking social media, he sees an address from Lavia is being posted all over. Wondering what this is, he clicks and turns his volume up just enough to hear it.

Two days ago, militants kidnapped eight people on a private trip. Last night, we, in retaliation, deployed 80 glidebombs from airbases in Kalnaka. We hit only strategic and governmental targets in the city of Aduab and surrounding towns. A screen behind the man changes from the Lavian seal to a satellite image of a burning refinery. By hitting this refinery and others like it, we cripple the little industry Sal-Baliz still has and cost them much more than any ransom would cost us. The image switches again, this time to a port. We arent foolish, we know where their fleet is, so we make an offer to the board at SummitOne. We know all you care about is money, as every company does, and ports are a very important part of your supply train, so would you rather expel these terrorist forces from your port, or have them sunk in it and have to spend tens of thousands removing their flaming hulls. And to the terrorists of Sal-Baliz, I know you hate us, but Im not sure youre stupid, so I'll offer this just in case. You can release the hostages like civil people, or we can keep launching cheap munitions into your remaining industry. Honestly, Id take freeing eight people over a complete halt to any manufacturing my country has. Hard to be on holy war when youd struggle to scrounge up enough bullets from your cratered factories.

The screen returns to the seal, and the man pauses for a little, thinking. We care for our fellow citizens, and the death of them would mean proportional destruction of the Sal-Baliz territory. Then after that, the recording ends.
Change of heart
